chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I go to the money-changer with dirhams and buy dinars from him, and he weighs for me more than my due, then I buy back my place with those dirhams. He said: 'There is no harm in it, but he should not weigh for you less than your due.'

key_terms.حَقِّي: My due/right (the exact amount owed or exchanged)
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy gold with silver if the seller gives extra weight as a gift or profit margin?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *fadl* (excess) in currency exchange when it serves as a commercial courtesy or profit margin, provided the transaction remains spot (*yadan bi yad*) and equitable. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits the money-changer to weigh out more gold than strictly required, as long as the subsequent repurchase of that gold with silver does not result in the customer receiving less than their due, thereby preventing hidden usury (*riba*). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between permissible market practices and exploitative debt-based usury.
